study_type_evidence.quote: ENF and PEG2k-ENF were subcutaneously administered at 1.7 μmol/kg (in physiological saline). Four animals per group were used.
The PEGylated peptide showed a 3.4-fold increase in the half-life against tryptic degradation

in_vitro_detail: Tryptic degradation stability and HIV fusion-inhibitory potency.

agents.sequence_source: PEPlife2 gives PEG2k-ENF THE SAME sequence as ENF; the 2 kDa PEG that accounts for the entire half-life difference is not encoded.

concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Pharmacokinetic analysis in Sprague-Dawley rats. ENF and PEG2k-ENF were subcutaneously administered at 1.7 μmol/kg (in physiological saline). Four animals per group were used.
concentration_time_figure.note: Non-compartmental analysis in WinNonlin 6.2; the caption defines T1/2 as the terminal half-life after pseudo-equilibrium.

bioanalytical_quote: The concentrations of ENF and the conjugate in plasma were determined using a known HPLC analysis.
notes: Both PEPlife2 values are consistent with the body: 1.5 ± 0.1 h for ENF and 16.1 ± 3.8 h for PEG2k-ENF, a 10.7-fold ratio matching the text's 'over 10-fold longer than that of ENF'. The per-agent figures come from the Figure 4B parameter panel. IDENTICAL SEQUENCE, 10-FOLD DIFFERENT LABEL: PEPlife2 assigns both agents the same enfuvirtide string, so the 2 kDa PEG that causes the entire effect is absent from the representation. Note also that both arms are subcutaneous with no intravenous comparator, and the body describes the conjugate as showing 'a slower but more sustained release profile from the injection site', so part of the difference is slower absorption rather than slower clearance.
